newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel to delay finance reform presentation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel to delay finance reform presentation.

text.p: A presidential panel examining financial reform in South Korea has delayed presenting its proposals to President Kim Young-sam until June 3, a commission official said on Thursday.

The official at the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said the postponement was needed because Kim was due to give a live television speech on Friday, the day when the panel had planned to make its presentation.
Kim was expected to address the nation on his 1992 campaign spending.

The 31-member commission's reform package to modernise South Korea's backward financial industry would cover the controversial issues of bank ownership, a unified financial supervisory body and central bank independence.
The panel was set up in January after President Kim said he would push forward with reform plans.
